Subject: Decision criteria & next steps for LLM inference evaluation

Hi Emma / Amit —

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time. Quick recap from our discovery so we're all aligned and to capture the open items: 

- Decision criteria you mentioned:
  - Latency: target p95 generation latency <= 200ms for the user-facing path (50–256 token responses).
  - Cost: target cost / 1M tokens to be competitive relative to your current vendor (you mentioned ~$120–150 per 1M tokens as a reference).
  - Deployment mode: prefer Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, but Procurement/Security want to evaluate Private (VPC) options if required by controls.
  - SLA: looking for a baseline 99.9% uptime and clear SLOs on tail latency + incident escalation playbook.

Open items / next steps we agreed on:
1) We'll send a short performance summary (attached) showing p50/p95/p99 for our recommended config and expected cost ranges.
2) Please share stakeholder mapping: economic buyer (CFO), procurement timelines, and Security/Legal contacts for the questionnaire.
3) If helpful, we can put together an initial mutual action plan (MAP) for procurement + security review timelines.

Attachments: Redwood_Perf_Summary_20270316.pdf (benchmarks + config notes)

Proposed next step: 30-min follow-up next week to walk through the perf numbers and map stakeholders. I'm available Wed/Thu 10–3 PT.

Thanks —

Thanks Emma — adding details below and attaching a draft SLA and SOC2 summary as requested.

Quick answers:
- Attachments: SOC2_Summary.pdf and SLA_Draft_Redwood_Finova_20270317.docx attached.
- Latency: Our recommended config for front-door (dedicated RTX-class nodes, dynamic batching with KV caching) typically hits ~120–160ms p95 for 50–256 tokens in our internal Finova-like workload. We've included p50/p95/p99 histograms in the perf summary.
- Cost tradeoffs: We outline two profiles in the perf summary: 1) Low-latency profile (reserved Dedicated nodes): higher fixed cost, lower tail latency; 2) Cost-optimized profile (quantized model + batching + prefix caching): ~25–35% lower token cost but p95 can increase by ~60–80ms depending on request distribution. I called that out since you mentioned the $120–150 / 1M tokens reference.
- Deployment modes: Dedicated (reserved) gives the predictability you want; Private (VPC) supports your data residency and additional controls but may add 2–3 weeks for network onboarding depending on your team. We call this out in the draft SLA/implementation notes.

Proposed MAP (short):
1) Technical validation: perf + privacy review (this week) — owners: Marissa + Rajiv
2) Security review: send questionnaire + SOC2 artifacts (1 week) — owner: Rajiv
3) Commercial intro and econ buyer briefing (after tech sign-off) — owner: Emma + Marissa
4) Procurement routing and legal redlines (4–6 weeks) — owner: Procurement

Would you be able to schedule a 30-min session with Rajiv and Laura (if available) next Tue/Wed? We'll bring Michael (contracts) and Monica (solutions) to answer deployment and SLA questions.

Thanks — attaching documents now.

Attachments: SLA_Draft_Redwood_Finova_20270317.docx; SOC2_Summary.pdf; Redwood_Perf_Summary_20270316.pdf
